content.text:
Reviewed the three open Aikido PRs. I recommend requesting changes on all three.

- [#88](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/88): The common cache loader still reads an unchecked path at [search_cache.go:188](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/b11b18cb458fdcb090cbd917237a3bbfd7c1aebb/internal/sem/search_cache.go#L188), bypassing the new guard. `Clean`/`Rel` also does not prevent symlink escapes. All checks pass, but no security tests were added.

- [#89](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/89): [ignore.go:179](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/534d742e7157e14b5fffb20a5819909a0134918d/internal/sem/ignore.go#L179) rejects Git’s standard linked-worktree `commondir` value (`../..`), so shared `.git/info/exclude` rules stop working. CI reproduces this failure. It also inconsistently rejects external absolute ignore files and valid session paths containing `..`.

- [#90](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/90): Shell injection remains in Gradle commands at [search_verify.go:965](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/blob/ee6303ff51aa03049440d8944a85f0a7981c2063/internal/sem/search_verify.go#L965), where repository-controlled module and class names remain unescaped. CI also fails numerous command-output assertions, and lint fails because the test file is unformatted.

I did not post reviews or modify the repository.
Fix all three. Also scan the codebase for similar issues that the PR addresses. Also, remove the [Aikido] from the PR titles.

I’m using the GitHub workflow again because this now includes branch pushes and PR metadata changes. I’ll fix each PR on its own branch, run a repository-wide path/shell-safety scan, push verified commits, and rename exactly:

- #88 → “AI Fix for Potential file inclusion attack via reading file”
- #89 → “AI Fix for Potential file inclusion attack via reading file”
- #90 → “Fix shell injection vulnerability in VERIFY build checks by escaping file paths”

The GitHub skill routes #89 and #90 through its CI-fix workflow, so I’m using that for log-based verification. I’m not using the new-PR publishing workflow because these are existing PR branches; commits will be pushed back to their current heads.

The three PR branches are now isolated. I’m assigning one repair owner per branch, each responsible for the original defect plus a repository-wide scan of the same issue class; I’ll independently review their diffs and verification before any push.

content.text: The GitHub app is read-only for PR metadata here (403), so the GitHub workflow is falling back to the authenticated `gh` CLI for the requested title edits. Branch work continues independently.

The broader scan is narrowing cleanly:

- Shell execution: only `internal/cli/verify.go` invokes `sh -c`, intentionally for an explicit command. The unsafe producer surface is `search_verify.go`; other subprocess sites pass argv directly.
- File reads: most accept explicit user paths or consume Git/WalkDir-enumerated files. The real untrusted relative-path boundary is source-line lookup from imported snapshots; cache paths are internally hash-derived. The repairs are being shaped around those actual boundaries instead of blanket `..` rejection.

All three titles are updated. The repair worktrees remain clean while the branch owners finish design audits; that is intentional here because two bot patches are mostly false-positive path checks, and I’m avoiding replacing them with another cosmetic guard. The scan has also confirmed no additional shell-string execution sites outside the VERIFY path.

The #89 design is settled: keep a real root-confined reader only at the imported-snapshot boundary using Go 1.24 `os.OpenRoot`, and remove the bot’s false-positive restrictions from caller-selected paths. Regression coverage will include traversal, symlinks, safe `..` filenames, worktrees, external ignore files, sessions, digests, and stats.

Implementation is now in motion on #89 and #90. For #88 I’ve bounded the design to one shared cache-read boundary: validate hash-derived object names, open beneath the cache root with `os.Root`, cover both snapshot and records caches, and leave atomic best-effort writes unchanged.

All three implementations are now applied locally, with tests being finalized. One worker hit a mixed Go toolchain cache before compilation; verification is being rerun through the repository-pinned Go 1.24.13 environment, which matches CI. No branch has been pushed yet.

The three repairs are now in their verification phase. The repository-wide scan found no additional shell-string execution path beyond generated VERIFY commands, and it narrowed the file-read hardening to cache boundaries plus imported snapshot source lookups; I’m reviewing those implementations and their adversarial tests before pushing anything.
